title: Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) Testing Framework — Overview and definition
t: Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) Testing Framework — Overview and definition
description: Tests control software against plant models entirely in software.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Tests control software against plant models entirely in software. A SIL framework compiles production control code unchanged and runs it against a simulated plant in lockstep, catching logic and timing bugs before hardware exists. Real implementations use Simulink SIL mode, ROS 2 with simulated time, and custom FMI-based harnesses. It checks determinism, worst-case execution time, and requirement coverage.

title: Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) Testing Framework — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Tests control software against plant models entirely in software.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) Testing Framework, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Production code compiled unchanged into the loop). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Production code compiled unchanged into the loop and Deterministic lockstep scheduling with simulated time. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation platform) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
